Happy Thursday! It's **Swin** again. In the very last days of the
interminable, _[extremely](https://zeteo.com/p/19-ways-trump-and-republicans-
are)_[high-stakes](https://zeteo.com/p/19-ways-trump-and-republicans-are) U.S.
midterm elections, things are not looking good… if you're a Republican or
**President Donald Trump**.

We'll see what happens on election night, but most signs are now pointing
toward stunning losses for the GOP, given that conservative politicians are so
inextricably wedded to Trump's agenda of unpopular war, mindless economic
destruction, unfettered corruption, and aberrant bloodshed and lawlessness.
It's hard to pick what GOP lawmakers and operatives are oh-so-very privately
steamed about the most, but if you talk to them, up high on that list is one
simple, two-syllable word:

**" Kansas."**

In today's '**First Draft** ,' we'll dig in on why. Plus, **Rep. Haley
Stevens** has an increasingly strange - and awful - way of showing her
supposed support for **Abdul El-Sayed** in the Michigan Senate election. Let's
read in.

If the Republican Party savagely eats it in the 2026 midterms (especially if
it's a defeat so
[humiliating](https://www.youtube.com/live/p_YVJJUfWDI?si=NNbYWQ9IyohM3sfg&t=1320)
it proves too hard [to steal](https://zeteo.com/p/inside-dems-plans-to-fight-
back-trump-ice-polls)), there is going to be a geyser of score-settling and
finger-pointing after election night. There is all but guaranteed to be a
gargantuan sum of anonymous or on-record intra-GOP sniping over who should be
scapegoated, with most participants being too cowardly to correctly and
publicly blame their god-emperor, Donald Trump.

The knives will be out for top Trump advisers who have, for different reasons,
made bitter and sometimes jealous enemies within their party structure. Think
[Susie Wiles, James Blair](https://zeteo.com/p/trumps-white-house-chief-of-
staff), MAGA-cogs like that - even if it wasn't _completely_ their fault.
Another Republican who keeps coming up in these types of discussions is Roger
Marshall, a Trump-backed senator from ruby-red, conservative Kansas.

[Subscribe now](https://zeteo.com/subscribe)

Marshall is running against pastor and Democrat Adam Hamilton in what has been
a shockingly close contest. If the Democratic Party flips a Senate seat in
_Kansas_ , of all places, it would be as good an indicator as any that the
2026 blue wave is more a blue biblical flood, crashing right into Trump's
authoritarian presidency and his party collaborators. A reminder: Trump won
Kansas by 16 points in 2024, and the state hasn't elected a Democratic senator
since… 1932!

Republican operatives working on competitive races and other key figures in
the party whom I've spoken to lately are cautiously optimistic (emphasis on
the adverb) that Marshall will squeak it out and keep that Kansas seat red.
Their Democratic counterparts say the same.

But even if Marshall wins, the damage is already done.
